The administration was directed to report back on options to commemorate Lyle Sanderson.
Including a recommendation or a recommended approach for future commemorative naming requests for interior civic facilities.
The original request was brought forward by a community delegation seeking to have competitive track at the Saskatoon Field House named in commemoration of Lyle Sanderson.
Lyle Sanderson's contribution to track and field university support and the broader Saskatoon community are substantial.
And administration recognizes the significance of Lyle Sanderson's legacy.
This report provides council with an evaluation of options for the specific naming request and addresses how future commemorative naming requests for interior civic facilities should be handled.

The position evaluated the policies that provide direction on civic naming or commemoration options and determine the current policies do not support commemorative naming of the Saskatoon House Field House track.
However, the policy related to the commemorations and monuments provides an existing and appropriate path to recognize Mr. Sanderson's legacy.
A key consideration in this report is city's ability to pursue future naming rights, sponsorships and partnership opportunities.
The city 2026 to 2029 strategic plan includes direction to enhance support for recreation facilities and programs to partnerships.
One of the key actions under that priority is to review sponsorship naming rights and advertising opportunities across existing and new facilities.
That work is already underway and administration is currently exploring naming rights and opportunities for the Shaw Center through a third party consultant.
Depending on the success of that work, similar approaches may be considered for other recreation facilities and spaces in the future.
The Saskatoon Field House, including interior spaces such as the track, have previously been identified as potential naming rights opportunities.
A 2018 assessment identified potential value for naming rights at the Field House track at approximately 27,500 dollars per year and market values have likely increased since that time.
For that reason, granting an exception to policy and permanently naming the track outside of a sponsorship or naming right process would mean for going a potential future revenue opportunity.
After reviewing the existing policies and revenue opportunities, administration has identified two potential options.
Option one is to decline the request to rename the Field House track while inviting the delegation to proceed with a commemoration that aligns with the city's commemorations and monuments policy.

This option would allow Mr. Sanderson's legacy to be recognized in a meaningful way at the Saskatoon Field House, while preserving the city's ability to explore future naming rights and opportunities for the track.
Option two is to approve the naming of the track as the Lyle Sanderson track.
This option would align directly with the delegations original request and preferred path forward.
However, it would also mean for going to potential revenue opportunity associated with naming rights for that track.
It may also create a precedent for future requests to name interior spaces within civic recreation facilities outside of existing policy.

The Lyle Sanderson delegation has indicated if they were granted commemorative naming rights at the track, they would also be interested in pursuing a commemoration or memorial for Lyle Sanderson as outlined in option one.

Administration is recommending that the delegation representing Lyle Sanderson naming committee be permitted to proceed with option one as outlined in the report and the future commemorative naming request for interior civic facilities be directed to existing policy options.
